name: TN-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent DesJarlais with large financial advantage
Democratic challenger underfunded with minimal cash
model.rationale: The district's Republican lean, DesJarlais's incumbency and roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge, and prediction markets near 93% Republican all point to a comfortable incumbent win, with no polling or expert ratings suggesting vulnerability.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending against DesJarlais, whose past personal controversies could resurface, would be the main signal of a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tennessee's 4th District leans firmly Republican, and incumbent Scott DesJarlais is seeking another term with the advantages that come with it. He has raised over half a million dollars and holds nearly half a million in cash, while Democratic nominee Victoria Broderick has raised under $60,000 and reports only about $8,500 on hand. No independent groups are active in the race on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 93% chance of holding the seat. A pair of independents with little funding are also on the ballot but are unlikely to alter the outcome materially.
